![Kayce Basques](https://web.dev/images/authors/kaycebasques.jpg) Kayce Basques [X](https://twitter.com/kaycebasques) [GitHub](https://github.com/kaycebasques) ![Sofia Emelianova](https://web.dev/images/authors/sofiayem.jpg) Sofia Emelianova [GitHub](https://github.com/sofiayem)

<br />

This page is a reference of features related to the Chrome DevTools Console. It assumes that you're
already familiar with using the Console to view logged messages and run JavaScript. If not, see [Get
Started](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console).

If you're looking for the API reference on functions like `console.log()` see [Console API
Reference](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/api). For the reference on functions like `monitorEvents()` see [Console Utilities API
Reference](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/utilities).

## Open the Console

You can open the Console as a [panel](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#panel) or as a [tab in the Drawer](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#drawer).

### Open the Console panel

Press <kbd>Control</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>J</kbd> or
<kbd>Command</kbd>+<kbd>Option</kbd>+<kbd>J</kbd> (Mac).

![The Console.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/the-console-6f950bdc19aaf.png)

To open the Console from the [Command Menu](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/command-menu), start typing `Console` and then run the **Show
Console** command that has the **Panel** badge next to it.

![The command for showing the Console panel.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/the-command-showing-con-f85c9a0f142ce.png)

### Open the Console in the Drawer

Press <kbd>Escape</kbd> or click **Customize And Control DevTools**
![Customize And Controls DevTools.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/customize-controls-devto-a11c847ca4f1f.svg) and then
select **Show Console Drawer**.

![Show Console Drawer.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/show-console-drawer-59809ff304585.png)

The Drawer pops up at the bottom of your DevTools window, with the **Console** tab open.

![The Console tab in the Drawer.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/the-console-tab-the-draw-4018fc60af19b.png)

To open the Console tab from the [Command Menu](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/command-menu), start typing `Console` and then run the **Show
Console** command that has the **Drawer** badge next to it.

![The command for showing the Console tab in the Drawer.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/the-command-showing-con-9f07d7c3a4bbd.png)

### Open Console Settings

Click ![Settings.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/settings-15d0f4489b69f.svg) **Console Settings** in the top-right corner of the **Console**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Key point:** Not to be confused with ![Settings.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/settings-02c6e6051a9dd.svg) **DevTools Settings** above and next to the ![Three-dot menu.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/three-dot-menu-a5764db14d971.svg) three-dot menu.

![Console Settings.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/console-settings-8f1c503823667.png)

The links below explain each setting:

- [**Hide network**](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#network)
- [**Preserve log**](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#persist)
- [**Selected context only**](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#filtercontext)
- [**Group similar messages in console**](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#group)
- [**Show CORS errors in console**](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#cors-errors)
- [**Log XMLHttpRequests**](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#xhr)
- [**Eager evaluation**](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#eagereval)
- [**Autocomplete from history**](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#autocomplete)

### Open the Console Sidebar

Click **Show Console Sidebar**
![Show Console Sidebar.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/show-console-sidebar-97d49cca04c9f.png) to show
the Sidebar, which is useful for filtering.

![Console Sidebar.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/console-sidebar-c42a801355417.png)

## View messages

This section contains features that change how messages are presented in the Console. See [View
messages](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console#view) for a hands-on walkthrough.

### Disable message grouping

[Open Console Settings](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#settings) and disable **Group similar** to disable the Console's default message
grouping behavior. See [Log XHR and Fetch requests](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#xhr) for an example.

### View messages from breakpoints

The **Console** marks messages triggered by breakpoints in the following way:

- `console.*` calls in [conditional breakpoints](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/javascript/breakpoints#conditional-loc) with an orange question mark `?`
- [Logpoint](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/javascript/breakpoints#log-loc) messages with pink two dots `..`

![The Console marks messages created by conditional breakpoints and logpoints.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/the-console-marks-message-1a9ce608a9866.png)

To jump to the [inline breakpoint editor](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/javascript/breakpoints#edit-breakpoints) in the **Sources** panel, click the anchor link next to the breakpoint message.

### View stack traces

The **Console** automatically captures stack traces for errors and warnings. A stack trace is a history of function calls (frames) that led to the error or warning. The **Console** shows them in reverse order: the latest frame is at the top.

To view a stack trace, click the ![Expand.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/expand-e745f93533c9a.svg) expand icon next to an error or warning.

![Stack traces.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/stack-traces-b6505c8b94793.png)

#### View error causes in stack traces

The **Console** can show you chains of [error causes](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Error/cause) in the stack trace, if any.

To make debugging easier, you can [specify error causes](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Error/cause#examples) when catching and rethrowing errors. As the **Console** walks up the cause chain, it prints each error stack with a `Caused by:` prefix, so you can find the original error.

![A chain of error causes prefixed with 'Caused by:' in the stack trace.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/chain-of-causes.png)

#### View async stack traces

If supported by the framework you are using or when directly using browser scheduling primitives, such as `setTimeout`, DevTools can trace async operations by linking both parts of the async code together.

In this case, the stack trace shows the "full story" of the async operation.

![Async stack trace.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/async-stack-trace-a2ff4e3f55d8d.png)

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Key point:** DevTools implements this "Async Stack Tagging" feature based on the `console.createTask()` API method. DevTools encourages frameworks and abstractions to use this API. For example, [Angular supports this feature](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/devtools-better-angular-debugging#the_async_stack_tagging_api_in_angular).

#### Show known third-party frames in stack traces

When source maps include the `ignoreList` field, by default, the **Console** hides from stack traces the third-party frames from sources generated by bundlers (for example, webpack) or frameworks (for example, Angular).

To view the full stack trace including third-party frames, click **Show N more frames** at the bottom of the stack trace.

![Show N more frames.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/show-n-more-frames-54f6f596dd5ba.png)

To always view the full stack trace, disable the ![Settings.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/settings-0eb8492a23f31.svg) **Settings** \> **Ignore List** \> **Automatically add known third-party scripts to ignore list** setting.

![Automatically add known third-party scripts to ignore list.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/automatically-add-known-t-9b48da4945eac.png)

### Log XHR and Fetch requests

[Open Console Settings](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#settings) and enable **Log XMLHttpRequests** to log all `XMLHttpRequest` and
`Fetch` requests to the Console as they happen.

![Logging XMLHttpRequest and Fetch requests.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/logging-xmlhttprequest-f-402c461943e5f.png)

The top message in the example above shows the Console's default grouping behavior. The example below shows
how the same log looks after [disabling message grouping](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#group).

![How the logged XMLHttpRequest and Fetch requests look after ungrouping.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/how-logged-xmlhttpreques-7b7ad3bf3afc3.png)

### Persist messages across page loads

By default the Console clears whenever you load a new page. To persist messages across page loads,
[Open Console Settings](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#settings) and then enable the **Preserve Log** checkbox.

### Hide network messages

By default the browser logs network messages to the **Console**. For example, the top message in
the following example represents a 404.

![A 404 message in the Console.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/a-404-message-the-consol-b9d6dc3606ad.png)

To hide network messages:

1. [Open Console Settings](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#settings).
2. Enable the **Hide Network** checkbox.

### Show or hide CORS errors

The **Console** can show [CORS errors](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/CORS/Errors) if network requests fail due to [Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS)](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/CORS).

To show or hide CORS errors:

1. [Open Console Settings](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#settings).
2. Check or clear the **Show CORS errors in the console** checkbox.

![Show CORS errors in the console.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/show-cors-errors-the-con-897bd466a9a6f.png)

If the console is set to show CORS errors and you encounter them, you can click the following buttons next to errors:

![Network and Issues buttons.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/network-issues-buttons-3c573df61de8c.png)

- ![Network.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/network-d77dd91a125b1.png) to open the request with a CORS-related `TypeError` in the **Network** panel.
- ![Issues.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/issues-c6a3845ddedc9.png) to get a [potential solution on the **Issues** tab](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/issues#view-issues).

## Filter messages

There are many ways to filter out messages in the Console.

### Filter out browser messages

[Open the Console Sidebar](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#sidebar) and click **User Messages** to only show messages that came from the
page's JavaScript.

![Viewing user messages.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/viewing-user-messages-fd80007bd49da.png)

### Filter by log level

DevTools assigns most of `console.*` methods severity levels.

There are four levels:

- `Verbose`
- `Info`
- `Warning`
- `Error`

For example, `console.log()` is in the `Info` group, whereas
`console.error()` is in the `Error` group. The [Console API Reference](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/api) describes the severity
level of each applicable method.

Every message that the browser logs to the Console has a severity
level too. You can hide any level of messages that you're not interested in. For example, if you're
only interested in `Error` messages, you can hide the other 3 groups.

Click the **Log Levels** drop-down to enable or disable `Verbose`, `Info`, `Warning` or `Error`
messages.

![The Log Levels drop-down.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/the-log-levels-drop-down-4b8620c9333db.png)

You can also filter by log level by ![Show Console Sidebar.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/show-console-sidebar-9781ba1d8989.png) [opening the Console Sidebar](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#sidebar) and then clicking **Errors** ,
**Warnings** , **Info** , or **Verbose**.

![Using the Sidebar to view warnings.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/using-sidebar-view-warn-6dcc0bf41b4ea.png)

### Filter messages by URL

Type `url:` followed by a URL to only view messages that came from that URL. After you type `url:`
DevTools shows all relevant URLs.

![A URL filter.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/a-url-filter-884c666b78573.png)

Domains also work. For example, if `https://example.com/a.js` and
`https://example.com/b.js` are logging messages, `url:https://example.com` enables you to focus on
the messages from these 2 scripts.

To hide all messages from a specified URL, type `-url:` followed by the URL, for example, `https://b.wal.co`. This is a negative URL filter.

![A negative URL filter. DevTools is hiding all messages that match the specified URL.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/a-negative-url-filter-de-f075a3627a864.png)

You can also show messages from a single URL by [opening the Console Sidebar](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#sidebar), expanding the
**User Messages** section, and then clicking the URL of the script containing the messages you want
to focus on.

![Viewing the messages from a specific script.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/viewing-messages-a-spec-4402844952b06.png)

### Filter out messages from different contexts

Suppose that you've got an ad on your page. The ad is embedded in an `<iframe>` and is generating a
lot of messages in your Console. Because this ad is in a different [JavaScript context](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#context), one way
to hide its messages is to [open Console Settings](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#settings) and enable the **Selected Context Only**
checkbox.

### Filter out messages that don't match a regular expression pattern

Type a regular expression such as `/[foo]\s[bar]/` in the **Filter** text box to filter out any
messages that don't match that pattern. Spaces are not supported, use `\s` instead. DevTools checks if the pattern is found in the message text
or the script that caused the message to be logged.

For example, the following filters out all messages that don't match `/[gm][ta][mi]/`.

![Filtering out any messages that don't match /\[gm\]\[ta\]\[mi\]/.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/filtering-any-messages-82d76b2bac549.png)

## Search for text in logs

To search for text in log messages:

1. To open a built-in search bar, press <kbd>Command</kbd>+<kbd>F</kbd> (Mac) or <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>F</kbd> (Windows, Linux).
2. In the bar, type your query. In this example the query is `legacy`. ![Typing a query.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/typing-query-2bd59434cd993.png) Optionally, you can:
   - Click ![Match case.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/match-case-f13fa89cd5c1d.png) **Match Case** to make your query case-sensitive.
   - Click ![RegEx button.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/regex-button-7c7a899b3d964.png) **Use Regular Expression** to search using a RegEx expression.
3. Press <kbd>Enter</kbd>. To jump to previous or next search result, press the up or down button.

## Run JavaScript

This section contains features related to running JavaScript in the Console. See [Run
JavaScript](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console#javascript) for a hands-on walkthrough.

### String copy options

The console outputs strings as valid JavaScript literals by default. Right-click an output and choose between three copy options:

- **Copy as JavaScript literal**. Escapes appropriate special characters and wraps the string in either single quotes, double quotes, or backticks depending on the content.
- **Copy string contents**. Copies the exact raw string to the clipboard, including new lines and other special characters.
- **Copy as JSON literal**. Formats the string to valid JSON.

![The copy options.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/the-copy-options-63b12751edae3.png)

### Re-run previous expressions and clear history

Press the <kbd>Up Arrow</kbd> key to cycle through the history of JavaScript expressions that you
ran earlier in the **Console** . Press <kbd>Enter</kbd> to run that expression again.

To clear the console history, right-click an empty space in the **Console** and select **Clear console history** from the context menu.

### Clear, copy, and save messages

To clear the **Console** window, do one of the following:

- Click block **Clear console** in the action bar at the top.
- Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>L</kbd> or <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>K</kbd>.
- Right-click an empty space in the **Console** and select **Clear console** from the context menu.

![The right-click context menu.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/clear-console.png)

From the context menu, you can also:

- **Copy console** : Copy all current messages to clipboard, but not the [history of previous commands](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#history).
- **Save as...** : Save all current messages to a plaintext `.log` file.

### Watch an expression's value in real-time with Live Expressions

If you find yourself typing the same JavaScript expression in the Console repeatedly, you might find
it easier to create a **Live Expression** . With **Live Expressions** , you type an expression once and
then pin it to the top of your Console. The value of the expression updates in near real-time. See
[Watch JavaScript Expression Values In Real-Time With Live Expressions](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/live-expressions).

### Disable Eager Evaluation

As you type JavaScript expressions in the Console, **Eager Evaluation** shows a preview of that
expression's return value. [Open Console Settings](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#settings) and disable the **Eager Evaluation** checkbox
to turn off the return value previews.

### Trigger user activation with evaluation

[User activation](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/user-activation) is the state of a browsing session that depends on user actions. An "active" state means the user is currently interacting with the page or has interacted since page load.

To trigger user activation with any evaluation, [open Console Settings](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#settings) and
check ![Checkbox.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/checkbox-7c5de7ca3499a.svg) **Treat code evaluation as user action**.

### Disable autocomplete from history

As you type out an expression, the Console's autocomplete popup shows expressions that you ran
earlier. These expressions are prepended with the `>` character. In the following example, DevTools earlier evaluated `document.querySelector('a')` and `document.querySelector('img')`.

![The autocomplete popup showing expressions from history.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/the-autocomplete-popup-sh-d3de9cbaf1506.png)

[Open Console Settings](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#settings) and
disable the **Autocomplete From History** checkbox to stop showing expressions from your history.

### Select JavaScript context

By default the **JavaScript Context** drop-down is set to **top** , which represents the main
document's [browsing context](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Glossary/Browsing_context).

![The JavaScript Context drop-down.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/the-javascript-context-dr-83ecda0d539c.png)

Suppose you have an ad on your page embedded in an `<iframe>`. You want to run JavaScript in order
to tweak the ad's DOM. To do this, you first need to select the ad's browsing context from the
**JavaScript Context** drop-down.

![Selecting a different JavaScript context.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/selecting-different-java-26cfea133c9d3.png)

## Inspect object properties

The **Console** can display an interactive list of properties of a JavaScript object you specify.

To browse the list, type the object name into the **Console** and press <kbd>Enter</kbd>.

To inspect the properties of DOM objects, follow the steps in [View the properties of DOM objects](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/dom/properties).

### Spot own and inherited properties

The **Console** sorts own object properties first and highlights them in bold font.

![Displaying object properties.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/displaying-object-propert-bd8db852a5889.png)

Properties inherited from the prototype chain are in regular font. The **Console** displays them on the object itself by evaluating the corresponding native accessors of built-in objects.

![Displaying inherited properties.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/displaying-inherited-prop-bf6fdacca9697.png)

### Evaluate custom accessors

By default, DevTools doesn't evaluate accessors you create.
![Custom accessor.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/custom-accessor-4d4daa1a09a6f.png)
To evaluate a custom accessor on an object, click `(...)`.
![Evaluated custom accessor.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/evaluated-custom-accessor-8829433f2e52c.png)

### Spot enumerable and non-enumerable properties

Enumerable properties are bright in color. Non-enumerable properties are muted.
![Enumerable and non-enumerable properties.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/enumerable-non-enumerabl-3837a25650013.png)
Enumerable properties can be iterated over with the `for ... in` loop or `Object.keys()` method.

### Spot private properties of class instances

The **Console** designates [private properties](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Classes/Public_class_fields) of class instances with a `#` prefix.

![Private property of a class instance.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/private-property-a-class-a302d4ca8a28b.png)

The **Console** can also autocomplete private properties even when you evaluate them ouside the class scope.

![Private property autocompletion.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/private-property-autocomp-ab8bb3964dfe.png)

### Inspect internal JavaScript properties

Borrowing the [ECMAScript notation](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-object-internal-methods-and-internal-slots), the **Console** encloses some properties internal to JavaScript in double square brackets. You can't interact with such properties in your code. However, it might be useful to inspect them.

You might see the following internal properties on different objects:

- Any object has a `[[Prototype]]`. ![Object prototype.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/object-prototype-d70846e61d721.png)
- Primitive wrappers have a `[[PrimitiveValue]]` property. ![Primitive values.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/primitive-values-51d1434a7cc8a.png)
- [`ArrayBuffer` objects](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/ArrayBuffer) have the following properties:
  - [`[[Int8Array]]`, `[[Uint8Array]]`, `[[Int16Array]]`, `[[Int32Array]]`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#table-the-typedarray-constructors)
  - [`[[ArrayBufferByteLength]]`, `[[ArrayBufferData]]`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-properties-of-the-arraybuffer-instances) ![ArrayBuffer and view objects.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/arraybuffer-view-objects-2189af3ff2a89.png)

    > [!IMPORTANT]
    > **Key point:** To [inspect a JavaScripts ArrayBuffer](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/memory-inspector) that a view object refers to, click the ![Memory icon.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/memory-icon-f453712cca57d.svg) button.

- In addition to `ArrayBuffer`-specific properties, `WebAssembly.Memory` objects have a `[[WebAssemblyMemory]]` property. ![WebAssemblyMemory object.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/webassemblymemory-object-2ba8b7fce18de.png)
- [Keyed collections](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-keyed-collections) (maps and sets) have an `[[Entries]]` property that contains their keyed entries. ![Keyed collections.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/keyed-collections-c349565c5c276.png)
- [`Promise` objects](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise) have the following properties:
  - [`[[PromiseState]]`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-properties-of-the-promise-prototype-object): pending, fulfilled, or rejected
  - [`[[PromiseResult]]`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-properties-of-the-promise-prototype-object): `undefined` if pending, `<value>` if fulfilled, `<reason>` if rejected ![Promise object.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/promise-object-4f1dbb08568e2.png)
- [`Proxy` objects](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Proxy) have the following properties: `[[Handler]]` object, `[[Target]]` object, and `[[isRevoked]]` (switched off or not). ![Proxy object.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/proxy-object-a629ca66c8f9a.png)

### Inspect functions

In JavaScript, functions are also objects with properties. However, if you type a function name into the **Console**, DevTools calls it instead of displaying its properties.

To view function properties internal to JavaScript, use the [console.dir()](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/api#dir) command.

![Inspecting properties of a function.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/inspecting-properties-a-9a5db0dd363c9.png)

Functions have the following properties:

- `[[FunctionLocation]]`. A link to the line with the function definition in a source file.
- `[[Scopes]]`. Lists values and expressions the function has access to. To inspect function scopes during debugging, see [View and edit local, closure, and global properties](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/javascript/reference#scope).
- [Bound functions](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_objects/Function/bind) have the following properties:
  - `[[TargetFunction]]`. The target of `bind()`.
  - `[[BoundThis]]`. The value of `this`.
  - `[[BoundArgs]]`. An array of function arguments. ![Bound function.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/bound-function-d7efcafc4e44a.png)
- [Generator functions](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Statements/function*) are marked with a `[[IsGenerator]]: true` property. ![Generator function.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/generator-function-87084b5308578.png)
- Generators return iterator objects and they have following properties:
  - `[[GeneratorLocation]]`. A link to a line with the generator definition in a source file.
  - `[[GeneratorState]]`: `suspended`, `closed`, or `running.`
  - `[[GeneratorFunction]]`. The generator that returned the object.
  - `[[GeneratorReceiver]]`. An object that receives the value. ![Iterator object.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/iterator-object-3140d0593e6f.png)

## Clear the Console

You can use any of the following workflows to clear the Console:

- Click **Clear Console** ![Clear.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/reference/image/clear-fbf5ccade18c4.svg).
- Right-click a message and then select **Clear Console**.
- Type `clear()` in the Console and then press <kbd>Enter</kbd>.
- Call `console.clear()` from your webpage's JavaScript.
- Press <kbd>Control</kbd>+<kbd>L</kbd> while the Console is in focus.
